## 2026-06-03 - Standalone SDK Toolchain Guard Preflights

- Added version-aware JDK 21 resolution to the standalone privacy, Kagemusha
  recursive spend, and SoraFS pin-register JVM SDK guard scripts. Each script
  now rejects inherited non-21 `JAVA_HOME` values, accepts a documented
  per-lane Java-home override variable, falls back to local/macOS/
  Homebrew/Linux JDK 21 homes when no Java home is set, exports the resolved
  Java home, and prints `java -version` before Gradle or `javac` runs.
- Extended the privacy, Kagemusha, and SoraFS meta-guards so they fail closed
  if the JVM scripts lose the `is_java_21_home` resolver, Java 21 version
  matcher, selected Java version evidence, or documented Java-home override
  variable.
- Wired the JVM JDK 21 script drift negative controls into the privacy,
  Kagemusha, and SoraFS SDK guard workflows, so CI now proves that dropping the
  traced `java -version` evidence or renaming a documented Java-home override
  variable is detected before the main guard runs.
- Tightened the privacy, Kagemusha, and SoraFS JavaScript meta-tests so they
  derive required workflow negative-control modes and pull-request path
  coverage from each guard script's command/path inventories. A new
  negative-control mode or guarded file path now has to appear in the workflow
  before the meta-test can pass, including root-level docs such as
  `status.md` and `roadmap.md`, while Kagemusha directory globs such as
  `crates/connect_norito_bridge/include/**` still count as covering individual
  guarded files underneath the directory. The same meta-tests now reject
  duplicate negative-control mode entries and duplicate guarded path inventory
  entries in the guard inventories.
- Added workflow-level adversarial controls that mutate the JVM jobs away from
  Temurin or Java 21; privacy, Kagemusha, and SoraFS guards now reject both
  setup-action deletion and wrong Java distribution/version pins.
- The standalone Swift SDK parse scripts now print `"${SWIFTC_BIN}" --version`
  before parsing. Kagemusha now uses an overrideable selected compiler like the
  privacy script, and the SoraFS script fails closed if `swiftc` is unavailable
  instead of silently skipping the parse. The privacy, Kagemusha, and SoraFS
  guards and workflows have negative controls proving missing Swift compiler
  evidence is rejected.
- Added JVM setup-order controls for privacy and SoraFS so their workflow
  guards now reject running the JVM SDK test command before Java setup. The
  Python privacy exact-research-source hostile fixture now includes the earlier
  source-referenced metadata, so it reaches the intended missing exact-source
  URL rejection.
- Added matching C# workflow controls across privacy, Kagemusha, and SoraFS:
  the guards now require `actions/setup-dotnet@v4` with `dotnet-version: 8.0.x`
  inside the C# job and reject running C# SDK tests before .NET setup.
- The standalone C# SDK scripts now print `"${DOTNET_BIN}" --version` before
  running filtered `dotnet test`, and the privacy, Kagemusha, and SoraFS
  meta-guards have negative controls proving that dropping this selected-SDK
  evidence is rejected.
- The standalone C# SDK scripts now also reject any selected SDK version outside
  `8.0.x` before restore/test. Privacy, Kagemusha, and SoraFS guards and
  workflows include script-drift negative controls that mutate the matcher to
  `7.0.*` and require rejection.
- Added JavaScript workflow controls across privacy, Kagemusha, and SoraFS:
  the guards now require Node 20, the package-lock cache-dependency path, and
  Node setup before `npm ci`.
- The standalone JavaScript SDK runners now print `"${NODE_BIN}" --version`
  before running focused `node --test` suites. Kagemusha recursive spend now
  uses `ci/check_kagemusha_recursive_spend_js_sdk.sh` instead of an inline
  workflow command, and privacy, Kagemusha, and SoraFS guards have
  script-drift negative controls proving that dropping selected-Node-version
  evidence is rejected.
- Added Python workflow controls across privacy, Kagemusha, and SoraFS: the
  guards now require Python 3.11 and setup-python before the Python SDK test
  command. JS/Python privacy hostile fixtures were tightened so research-stage
  tests satisfy earlier source/readiness metadata gates before asserting the
  intended failure.
- The standalone Python SDK scripts now print `"${PYTHON_BIN}" --version` and
  `"${VENV_DIR}/bin/python" --version` before running pytest. Privacy,
  Kagemusha, and SoraFS guards have script-drift negative controls proving that
  dropping the venv Python version evidence, documented override variable, or
  Python 3.11 resolver is rejected.

  fail-closed checks into one CI entrypoint. The guard audits its workflow path
  coverage, runs the JavaScript cross-SDK privacy parity/native tests, and runs
  the Python privacy catalog, native-registry, crypto, and component-builder
  adversarial tests from a temporary venv.
- Added `.github/workflows/pr_privacy_sdk_guard.yml` so privacy native host,
  SDK bridge, component builder, cross-SDK parity test, docs, roadmap, and
  status changes trigger the guard on pull requests.
- Documented the generic raw-Norito privacy bridge, operation-specific result
  schemas, 64 MiB native cap, and `privacy-production-gate-v1` fail-closed
  boundary across the Swift, Java, Kotlin, C#, JavaScript, and Python SDK
  READMEs. The guard now requires those README files in workflow path filters
  and checks for the shared fail-closed contract plus each SDK's public API
  names.
- Strengthened the JavaScript FFI parity assertion so JS native privacy output
  decoding must pass `privacyExpectedResultSchemaByte(operation)` into the
  Norito archive validator instead of only checking generic frame shape.
- Validation passed:

## 2026-06-02 Reserved-lineage SDK and adversarial CI gates

- Added `ci/check_kagemusha_recursive_spend_sdk_parity.sh`, a source-only ABI-6
  parity gate for recursive Kagemusha Reserved-lineage. It checks all eight C
  bridge symbols, C header declarations, JNI exports for Android and Kotlin
  package names, Node NAPI exports, Swift, Java, Kotlin, JavaScript, Python,
  package-root re-exports, PyO3 host exports, and C# public helpers,
  availability probes, fail-closed witnessless helpers, and shared constants
  (`ABI_VERSION = 6`, witnessless max hops `0`, previous proof open-envelope
  count `1`, and max bytes `8 MiB`). The fail-closed helper body checks now
  require exact direct-false implementations across Rust, Swift, Kotlin,
  Android Java, JavaScript, Python, and C#; JavaScript is checked in Node
  source, Node dist, browser source, and browser dist files so stale packaged
  helpers cannot reopen witnessless redeem or append.
- Wired the SDK parity gate into `.github/workflows/pr_kagemusha_payload_bench.yml`
  before the payload benchmark and expanded workflow path filters to include
  every SDK source/declaration file the guard scans. The parity gate now
  verifies those workflow path filters directly, so adding or removing a
  guarded SDK source without CI coverage fails the source-only check.
- The workflow path filters now also include the recursive-spend native crate
  manifests for the C bridge, JavaScript NAPI host, and Python PyO3 host
  (`crates/connect_norito_bridge/Cargo.toml`,
  `crates/iroha_js_host/Cargo.toml`, and
  `python/iroha_python/iroha_python_rs/Cargo.toml`). The SDK parity gate
  enforces those manifest paths, so feature/dependency metadata changes cannot
  bypass the ABI-6 guard.
- Expanded the same workflow path filters to include every SDK test file that
  the fail-closed policy guard scans, so test-only removal of null, unknown,
  maximum, negative, or non-integer helper edge cases still triggers the guard.
  The policy guard now verifies those workflow path filters directly as well.
- Extended `ci/check_kagemusha_recursive_spend_policy.sh` so the fail-closed
  policy also requires the existing adversarial Reserved-lineage tests to stay
  present. The source gate now protects coverage for witnessless rejection,
  record-backed multi-hop redeem, malformed lineage witnesses, missing,
  duplicate, and unreferenced verifier records, scalar-projection splices,
  previous-proof count mismatches, and forged multi-hop one-hop verifier-slice
  metadata. It now also protects the original core ISI mint path in
  `crates/iroha_core/src/smartcontracts/isi/offline.rs`: semantic recursive
  spend redemption must reject before mint, rejected redeems must not consume
  nullifiers or credit public balances, Reserved-lineage verifier-slice profiles
  must fail before mint, adversarial lineage verifier records must reject, and
  amount/final-proof binding mismatches must stay covered. The same source gate
  protects the JavaScript NAPI host and Python PyO3 host adversarial redemption
  tests at the native request-builder boundary: semantic-profile redemption,
  amount mismatches, missing anchors, missing or zero redeem verifier-key
  commitments, forged lineage verifier records, malformed lineage witnesses,
  missing verifier-slice columns, and witnessless Reserved-lineage requests. It
  now also pins the SDK helper edge-case tests for null/empty or unknown circuit
  ids, maximum hop counts, negative hop counts, and non-integer hop counts where
  the language surface permits them.
- Tightened the same policy guard to pin the public verify-result flags for
  recursive spend verification. Core, bridge, JavaScript host, and Python host
  coverage must keep returning `witnessless_redeem_supported = false` and
  `lineage_witness_required_for_redeem = true` for invalid, missing-record,
  wrong-record, empty-record, trusted-setup, STARK, and multi-hop
  Reserved-lineage cases, and the core verifier must continue deriving the
  public flags from the Rust fail-closed witnessless helper.
- Added built-in negative-control modes to
  `ci/check_kagemusha_recursive_spend_policy.sh`; one mutates an SDK edge-case
  token in memory, and one removes a guarded workflow path in memory. Each mode
  succeeds only if the fail-closed policy guard detects the drift.
- Added further policy negative controls for core ISI workflow-path removal and
  verify-result flag drift. These make path-filter omissions for the original
  mint-path file and accidental reopening of the public witnessless redeem flag
  fail source-only CI before any benchmark or proof test runs.
- Added a synthetic self-test mode to
  `ci/check_kagemusha_recursive_spend_payload_bench.sh` and wired it into the
  Kagemusha payload workflow before the real Criterion benchmark. The self-test
  reduces synthetic no-growth bundle and transition-profile Criterion output
  under a temporary directory with `SKIP_BENCH=1`, proving the reducer writes
  summary and TSV artifacts without invoking Cargo.
- Added payload benchmark negative controls for D2D payload growth, append
  transition-profile growth, and missing transition-profile hop coverage. Each
  control creates synthetic Criterion output and succeeds only when the reducer
  rejects the drift with a specific diagnostic.
- Wired those payload reducer negative controls into the Kagemusha payload
  workflow before the real Criterion benchmark, and extended the fail-closed
  policy guard so the self-test plus all three negative-control commands must
  stay present before benchmarking.
- Extended the fail-closed policy guard's workflow path audit to include
  `ci/check_kagemusha_recursive_spend_payload_bench.sh` itself, so edits to the
  reducer/self-test/negative-control script cannot bypass the Kagemusha payload
  workflow.
- Extended that workflow path audit to include all Kagemusha CI guard scripts:
  `ci/check_connect_norito_bridge_header.sh`,
  `ci/check_kagemusha_recursive_spend_sdk_parity.sh`,
  `ci/check_kagemusha_recursive_spend_policy.sh`, and
  `ci/check_kagemusha_recursive_spend_payload_bench.sh`.
- Added a source-only execution-order check to the fail-closed policy guard for
  `RedeemKagemushaRecursive::execute`. The guard now pins the production redeem
  sequence so public-input binding, lineage admission or record-backed lineage
  verification, recursive proof verification, final redeem proof verification,
  and nullifier insertion all remain before `Mint::asset_numeric` and
  `mint.execute`. It also requires exactly one mint construction and one mint
  execution in that implementation, so an added early mint cannot bypass the
  existing ordered path.
- Wired the fast SDK parity and fail-closed policy negative controls into the
  Kagemusha payload workflow before the real benchmark. Both source guards now
  require those workflow commands, and each has a self-referential negative
  control proving that removal of a required negative-control command fails
  source-only CI.
- Pinned the workflow's main guard steps as exact commands before the real
  benchmark: header parity, SDK parity, and the fail-closed policy guard must
  all run as standalone `run:` commands. A negative control mutates the main SDK
  parity command while leaving the SDK negative-control block intact, proving
  the workflow cannot keep only negative controls and skip the real guard.
- Tightened the workflow command audit so payload reducer and policy
  negative-control commands must appear as executable workflow command lines,
  not merely as substrings in comments or unrelated text. Comment-only negative
  controls prove that commented-out commands no longer satisfy the guard.
- Tightened the SDK parity workflow command audit the same way: SDK parity
  negative controls must appear as executable workflow command lines before the
  real benchmark, and the main SDK parity guard must run as a standalone
  `run:` command before the benchmark. Comment-only and main-guard mutation
  negative controls prove commented SDK commands or a skipped main SDK guard no
  longer satisfy the guard.
- Expanded the SDK parity guard beyond raw native wrappers so it also pins the
  JavaScript and Python recursive-spend mode, selector normalization, selector
  support, append-proving, and previous-proof preflight helpers. A new SDK
  helper-surface negative control removes a high-level JavaScript selector
  helper from re-exports and proves the workflow fails closed.
- Refreshed the core chain-admission rustdoc and append diagnostic so the source
  no longer describes witnessless Reserved-lineage admission as available inside

  lineage verifier proves the hop chain in-circuit.
- Added `status.md` to the fail-closed documentation guard and Kagemusha payload
  workflow path audit. The guard now rejects stale status or doc claims that
  describe one-hop witnessless Reserved-lineage redemption as available, and a
  dedicated negative control mutates the status note back to a stale admission
  claim to prove the check fails closed.
- Changed the Kagemusha payload workflow to keep in-progress runs alive
  (`cancel-in-progress: false`) so long proof/benchmark evidence is not
  interrupted by a newer push. The fail-closed policy guard now pins that
  workflow setting and includes a negative control that flips it back to

  The workflow path audit now requires the `iroha_data_model` crate manifest
  and `kagemusha_recursive_spend_payload.rs`, and the source guard requires the

## 2026-06-02 Swift privacy request failure zeroization

- Hardened the Swift privacy native request-copy helper with an internal
  call-scoped clear observer used by tests, without changing the public privacy
  bridge API. The helper now exposes the already-cleared temporary request copy
  to the test closure after `clearTemporaryPrivacyRequestArchive` runs.
- Added a Swift XCTest that throws from the native-dispatch closure and verifies
  the copied Norito request archive is zeroed on unwind while the caller-owned
  archive remains unchanged.
- Broadened the Swift public privacy request-call negative test so malformed
  magic bytes, reserved header fields, unsupported flags, nonzero padding,
  checksum tampering, and short archives all fail before native dispatch.
- Broadened the JavaScript source and package-dist privacy-native request tests
  with the same adversarial malformed Norito request fixtures, and made both
  bindings fail the test if invalid build or verify requests reach native
  dispatch.
- Broadened the Python privacy-native request tests with matching malformed
  Norito request fixtures and a no-dispatch fake native, covering both bytes
  and bytearray request inputs before build or verify can cross into native
  code.
- Broadened the Java Android, Kotlin/JVM, and C# privacy-native request tests
  with matching malformed Norito request fixture loops. Java and Kotlin copy
  each malformed archive through build and verify paths; C# covers both the
  internal `CallProof` no-dispatch path and the public build/verify request
  guards.
- Tightened Java Android and Kotlin/JVM malformed-request tests to assert the
  `valid Norito V1 archive` diagnostic fragment, so a generic argument failure
  can no longer satisfy the no-dispatch path.
- Broadened the C# public `PrivacyCapabilitiesArchive` and
  `PrivacyProofResultArchive` wrapper tests so every adversarial malformed
  Norito archive fixture is rejected by both wrapper types, not just a short
  archive and one payload-tamper case.
- Added a JavaScript privacy FFI parity guard that enforces defensive native
  output-copy tests across JS source/dist, Python, Swift, Java Android,
  Kotlin/JVM, and C#. The guard requires tests to mutate native-owned output
  buffers after wrapper return/free and prove returned archives remain stable.
- Hardened the BOI Privacy Lab catalog gate so planned SDK entrypoints carrying
  fixture/mock names are filtered before they are surfaced to the runner. The
  BOI hostile-SDK metadata regression now proves DevFixture/mock planned proof
  names are removed while a legitimate research planned builder remains.
- Tightened the BOI Privacy Lab production gate so SDK-supplied production
  booleans, including `externalAudit`, are treated as untrusted until a row is
  explicitly BOI allowlisted. Audit-reference URLs are still preserved as
  metadata, but they no longer make a non-allowlisted row's audit gate look
  passed.
- Hardened BOI Privacy Lab amount handling so non-finite request amounts cannot
  leak into desktop JSON as `NaN`. Unavailable executions sanitize adversarial
  amounts to `0.0`, while available privacy flows reject non-finite or
  non-positive amounts before wallet setup or runner construction.
- Extended the JavaScript privacy FFI parity guard so Swift failure-path
  request zeroization plus Swift, JS, Python, Java Android, Kotlin/JVM, and C#
  malformed-request rejection are enforced across SDKs.
- Added browser-source and browser-dist JavaScript crypto regressions that keep
  native privacy and Kagemusha recursive-spend helpers as fail-closed stubs, and
  added package-wiring coverage proving browser catalogs continue to route
  privacy bridge availability through the browser-mapped `crypto.js` module
  instead of calling native FFI directly.
- Broadened JavaScript and Python privacy catalog validation so planned SDK
  entrypoints containing generic fixture or mock markers are rejected before
  they can be advertised as future production builders, matching the BOI runner
  fixture/mock filter.
- Hardened the JavaScript, Python, and BOI planned-entrypoint fixture/mock
  filters against punctuation-spliced markers such as `M-o-c-k` and
  `Dev.Proof.Fixture`, so obfuscated dev fixtures cannot be surfaced as planned
  production builders.
- Added matching production-gate regressions for executable SDK entrypoints
  carrying punctuation-spliced fixture markers, proving JS, Python, and BOI keep
  those rows fail-closed even when `implementationStage` claims
  `production-hardened`.
- Added JavaScript source, JavaScript package-dist, and Python privacy-native
  regressions for sliced byte-view request archives. Valid Norito archives are
  wrapped in hostile prefix/suffix bytes and passed as `Uint8Array`/`DataView`
  or `memoryview` slices; the tests prove only the selected slice reaches native
  dispatch, native output slices decode correctly, caller-owned buffers stay
  unchanged, and temporary copied request archives are still zeroed.
- Extended the JavaScript privacy FFI parity guard to require those sliced
  byte-view request tests across JS source, JS dist, and Python.
- Added matching JavaScript source, JavaScript package-dist, and Python
  privacy-native regressions for sliced native output archive views. All three
  native operations now return valid Norito archives from views embedded in
  hostile backing buffers, and the tests prove the wrappers decode only the
  selected view range and defensively copy the archive before the backing bytes
  are mutated.
- Extended the JavaScript privacy FFI parity guard to require the sliced native
  output view regressions across JS source, JS dist, and Python.
- Added Java Android, Kotlin/JVM, and C# privacy-native regressions where a
  hostile native callback mutates the copied proof request archive before
  returning. The tests prove caller-owned request archives remain unchanged and
  the temporary dispatch copies are still zeroed after return.
- Added the same hostile request-mutation regression to Swift by mutating the
  temporary request buffer through the native-boundary pointer in the XCTest.
  The test proves the caller-owned `Data` archive remains unchanged and the
  copied request buffer is still zeroed after dispatch.
- Extended the JavaScript privacy FFI parity guard so those hostile native
  request-mutation regressions are required across Swift, Java Android,
  Kotlin/JVM, and C#.

## 2026-06-02 Kagemusha recursive redemption fail-closed gate

- Filled the recursive redemption safety gap by disabling witnessless
  Reserved-lineage mint admission until the production recursive lineage
  verifier proves private-hop lineage and accumulator transitions in-circuit.
  The Rust data model and Swift, Kotlin/JVM, Android Java, JavaScript, Python,
  and C# SDK helpers now expose
  `KAGEMUSHA_RECURSIVE_SPEND_LINEAGE_WITNESSLESS_MAX_HOPS_V1 = 0`,
  `canRedeem...Witnessless(...) = false`, and
  `requires...LineageWitnessForRedeem(...) = true`.
- The redeem request public-binding gate now rejects witnessless
  Reserved-lineage requests with `lineage_witness` before native hosts or core
  ISI can mint public assets. Core still validates Reserved-lineage profile
  shape for diagnostics, then returns the explicit
  `witnessless chain admission is disabled` lineage-verifier diagnostic.
- Updated bridge, JS host, PyO3 host, SDK helper tests, and offline Kagemusha
  docs to match the fail-closed boundary. Record-backed lineage witnesses remain
  the online redemption path.
- Extended Rust and SDK helper tests with adversarial fail-closed inputs:
  unknown, empty, and null circuit ids where supported; negative, maximum, and
  non-integer hop counts where the language permits them; and maximum unsigned
  hop counts in Swift/C#. Every case keeps `canRedeem...Witnessless` false,
  `requires...LineageWitnessForRedeem` true, and witnessless append helpers
  false.
- Corrected stale offline Kagemusha docs and roadmap wording that implied an
  enabled Reserved-lineage redeem serialization path without a witness. Current
  public docs now state that no witnessless Reserved-lineage hop count serializes while
  `KAGEMUSHA_RECURSIVE_SPEND_LINEAGE_WITNESSLESS_MAX_HOPS_V1 = 0`.
- Added a public-doc policy guard to
  `javascript/iroha_js/test/kagemushaFfiContractParity.test.js` so active docs
  and SDK READMEs fail if they reintroduce forbidden witnessless
  Reserved-lineage redemption claims while the Rust max-hop constant remains
  zero.
- Added `ci/check_kagemusha_recursive_spend_policy.sh` and wired it into the
  Kagemusha payload workflow after the header parity check. The check validates
  the Rust fail-closed helpers, requires active docs/SDK READMEs to document the

## 2026-06-02 Kagemusha Reserved-lineage transition profile

- Added `KagemushaRecursiveSpendTransitionProfileV1` as the canonical Norito
  contract for the accumulator transition the Reserved-lineage circuit must
  reproduce in-circuit. The profile binds previous accumulator/proof artifact
  state, normalized hop index, current hop statement, current spendable note,
  verifier-witness and table-base preflight digests, verifier context, resulting
  accumulator digest, and resulting recursive public-input hash.
- Added builders and a digest helper for initial and append transition profiles.
  Append profiles normalize one-hop evidence fragments into the accumulated hop
  index, so a second offline hop hashes as hop `1` even though the transport
  fragment carries one local hop.
- Wired the core recursive spend init and append proof constructors to build,
  validate, digest, and compare the transition profile against the accumulator
  they are about to prove. Native ABI-6 bridge requests now cross the same
  Reserved-lineage accumulator-transition preflight used by fixtures/tests
  before any recursive spend bundle is emitted.
- Extended data-model tests with transition-profile Norito roundtrip/parity
  checks and adversarial mutation coverage across prior proof artifact fields,
  previous/current note fields, hop statement fields, verifier preflight digests,
  roots, accumulator outputs, and public-input hashes.
- Added a core fixture test for the proof-boundary preflight: initial and append
  transition profiles must match the exact emitted accumulator, and a forged
  accumulator digest/field splice is rejected before proof emission.
- Extended the recursive spend payload Criterion benchmark and CI reducer to
  record `kagemusha_recursive_spend_transition_profile_bytes` for the same
  1/2/3/5/8/13/21/34/55/64 hop set. CI still gates the constant-size D2D bundle
  archive separately, and now also rejects append transition-profile growth.
- Extended the data-model hop-count-independent payload-size test to track
  transition-profile Norito lengths and reject append profile growth across the
  same hop set.
- Added parser-only controls to the payload CI reducer so the constant-size
  gates can be tested from synthetic Criterion directories without starting a
  Cargo benchmark. Positive, missing-transition-profile, and append-profile
  growth parser cases were validated.
- Documented the transition profile as the SDK fixture/circuit preflight surface
  while witnessless Reserved-lineage admission remains disabled.
- Exposed the transition-profile and transition-profile-digest domain tags in
  Swift, Kotlin/JVM, Android Java, JavaScript/Node/browser, Python, and C# SDK
  helper surfaces so fixture generators and app code can identify the same
  Reserved-lineage circuit contract without duplicating Rust literals.
- Exposed raw-Norito transition-profile archive helpers through the native C
  bridge, Node NAPI host, Python PyO3 host, Swift, Android Java, Kotlin/JVM,
  JavaScript, Python, and C# SDKs. ABI-6 availability probes now require both
  `transition_profile_init` and `transition_profile_append`, so older native
  libraries fail closed instead of pretending the Reserved-lineage accumulator
  preflight is available.
- Updated the shipped `connect_norito_bridge.h` header used by
  `NoritoBridge.xcframework` so C/Swift packaging exports the two
  transition-profile entry points alongside the existing init/append,
  lineage-witness, verify, and redeem ABI-6 symbols.
- Added `ci/check_connect_norito_bridge_header.sh` and wired it into the
  Kagemusha payload workflow. The guard compares Rust recursive-spend C exports
  with the shipped header, requires the eight ABI-6 declarations, checks the
  umbrella header include, and syntax-checks C/C++ headers when compilers are
  available.
- Added `javascript/iroha_js/test/kagemushaFfiContractParity.test.js` so CI
  source-checks the ABI-6 recursive spend contract across the Rust C bridge,
  shipped C header, Node NAPI host, Swift, Android Java, Kotlin/JVM,
  JavaScript/Node/browser, Python/PyO3, and C# wrappers. The test also verifies
  that SDK availability probes require both transition-profile helpers instead
  of accepting a partial ABI-6 surface.
- Kept witnessless Reserved-lineage append/redeem helpers fail-closed; this is a
  circuit contract and fixture surface, not an admission enablement.
- Re-audited the remaining full witnessless Reserved-lineage gate. The current
  Halo2 path is still the one-hop verifier-slice circuit; multi-hop admission
  would require proving the previous recursive proof and accumulator transition
  in-circuit. Flipping the SDK/core constants without that circuit would be
  unsound, so the record-backed lineage witness remains required for online
  redemption.
- Updated Swift, Android Java, Kotlin/JVM, JavaScript, Python, and C# SDK
  READMEs so ABI-6 availability lists include transition-profile init/append
  and the docs consistently state the current witnessless max-hop value is `0`.

## 2026-06-02 Kagemusha Reserved-lineage transition audit

- Re-audited the current Reserved-lineage path before enabling multi-hop helper
  flags. The existing `kagemusha-recursive-spend-lineage-v1` key/prover path is
  still the one-hop verifier-slice: it composes the semantic public-input
  surface with one Pallas IPA verifier witness and rejects real append output.
- Confirmed that a sound multi-hop Reserved-lineage append cannot be completed by
  only composing a previous-proof verifier and the new hop verifier. The append
  proof must also prove the recursive spend accumulator transition in-circuit,
  including the PoseidonByteHasher/Norito preimages for proof-chain, verifier
  batch, table-base, lineage, nullifier, output, fold, and accumulator digests.
- Left witnessless append/redeem selector helpers fail-closed. Advertising hop
  2+ Reserved-lineage support before that transition gadget exists would let
  SDKs construct requests that the chain cannot safely admit.

    `connect_norito_bridge kagemusha_recursive_spend_redeem_bridge` proof job

  recursive lineage verifier circuit is wired.

  `KagemushaRecursiveSpendAppendRequestV1`. The field is reserved for the
  production witnessless Reserved-lineage append circuit so callers can supply
  the previous recursive proof's Halo2/Pasta opening material without changing
  the ABI shape again.
- Append request validation accepts legacy empty archives for semantic
  compatibility append. Native core proving now requires a non-empty
  previous-proof opening archive when the selected output proof circuit is
  Reserved-lineage, matching the SDK helper contract. Malformed or
  syntactically empty provided archives are still rejected at the data-model
  boundary.
- `KagemushaRecursiveSpendAppendRequestV1` now carries a defaulted
  `output_proof_circuit_id`. Missing or empty values preserve legacy ABI-6
  semantic append output, unsupported selectors are rejected at request
  validation, and Reserved-lineage output selectors require the previous-proof
  opening archive. The C bridge/JNI path, JavaScript NAPI host, and Python PyO3
  host now honor that selector instead of always passing the semantic recursive
  aggregation circuit id.
- Plumbed the new archive through the core recursive append API and the C bridge,
  JavaScript NAPI host, and Python PyO3 host. The core API now independently
  rejects malformed, missing-for-Reserved-lineage-output, or syntactically
  empty previous-proof opening archives even when callers bypass request-level
  validation. Required previous-proof archives are now preflighted as bounded
  Pallas IPA opening material: native core rejects missing or zero metadata,
  non-Pallas curves, version drift, archives over the 8 MiB
  `KAGEMUSHA_RECURSIVE_PREVIOUS_PROOF_OPEN_ENVELOPES_MAX_BYTES` cap before
  decode, opening-length/generator/round-count mismatches, archive over-count,
  and IPA proof tampering during witness derivation before append proving can
  start. Native append preflight now also requires exactly one previous-proof
  opening envelope and binds its verifier-key commitment, public-input schema
  hash, and recursive-proof domain tag to the previous recursive proof being
  folded, rejecting cross-proof opening-witness splices before the future
  multi-hop circuit is reached.
- Moved the same 8 MiB previous-proof archive cap into data-model append request
  validation, so Rust constructors, bridge request validation, and SDK-provided
  Norito request archives reject oversized material before decode. Exposed the
  cap in Swift, Kotlin/JVM, Java Android, JavaScript/browser/Node, Python, and
  C# recursive-spend helpers with parity assertions.
- Tightened the data-model previous-proof archive validator to require exactly
  one `OpenVerifyEnvelope` whenever an archive is supplied, matching native
  append preflight. Exposed
  `KAGEMUSHA_RECURSIVE_PREVIOUS_PROOF_OPEN_ENVELOPES_REQUIRED_COUNT_V1` and
  SDK-equivalent constants across Swift, Kotlin/JVM, Java Android,
  JavaScript/browser/Node, Python, and C# with parity assertions.
- Added append-side branch helpers across the Rust data model and Swift,
  Kotlin/JVM, Java Android, JavaScript/Node/browser, Python, and C# SDKs:
  `canAppend...WitnesslessLineage(previousHopCount)` keeps the current
  one-hop verifier-slice bound visible to wallets, and
  `requires...PreviousProofOpenEnvelopesForAppend(outputCircuitId,
  previousHopCount)` tells callers when a future Reserved-lineage append must
  populate the previous recursive proof opening archive.
- Added append output-selector normalization helpers across the Rust data model
  and Swift, Kotlin/JVM, Java Android, JavaScript/Node/browser, Python, and C#.
  Missing or empty `output_proof_circuit_id` normalizes to semantic
  `kagemusha-recursive-aggregation-v1`; explicit
  `kagemusha-recursive-spend-lineage-v1` remains opt-in, and unknown selectors
  stay unmodified so request validation can reject them.
- Added validated Rust constructors for the recursive spend init, append, verify,
  and redeem request Norito types. The constructors fill legacy-compatible
  defaults, run the same public-binding validators used by the bridge, and now
  have positive plus adversarial coverage for malformed Pallas archives,
  previous-proof opening archives, semantic/Reserved-lineage verifier-record
  selection, and record-backed redeem witness binding.
- Updated the offline Kagemusha docs to describe the new append-request slot and
  its Norito archive contract, and updated the Swift, Kotlin, and Java Android
  SDK README sections that already document the recursive spend helper surface.
- Full witnessless multi-hop Reserved-lineage append/redeem remains the open
  circuit task: the current verifier-slice profile is still bounded to one hop,
  so larger hop counts must use the record-backed lineage witness path.

## 2026-06-02 Privacy catalog production-gate parity

- Added a JavaScript test that imports both `src` and checked-in `dist`
  privacy algorithm catalogs, loads the Python privacy catalog by file path,
  and compares their shared production-gate metadata. The guard fails if JS
  source, JS dist, or Python drift on algorithm id order, privacy criteria,
  verifier metadata, SDK entrypoints, planned entrypoints, production-ready
  flags, missing gate reasons, audit references, or duplicate/planned
  entrypoint overlap.
- Extended that guard to read the Java Android, Kotlin/JVM, Swift, and C#
  privacy native bridge source declarations and require their fail-closed
  missing production-gate reason sequence to match the catalog-derived
  canonical sequence.
- Extended the same guard to parse the Rust native
  `PRIVACY_ALGORITHM_ENTRIES` declarations in `connect_norito_bridge`,
  `iroha_js_host`, and `iroha_python_rs`. The test now locks native capability
  row order, proof families, backend families, executable SDK entrypoints, and
  planned entrypoints to the SDK catalog contract.
- The Python privacy catalog now exposes derived `backend_family` metadata for
  every row and rejects otherwise valid synthetic catalog rows whose algorithm
  id lacks backend-family registration. Python and JavaScript parity tests now
  compare native Rust backend families against that SDK catalog value instead
  of keeping backend selection as native-only metadata. The Python loader now
  also treats raw `backend_family` / `backendFamily` fields as derived metadata
  and rejects forged backend-family claims before descriptor enrichment.
- The JavaScript source and checked-in dist catalogs now expose the same
  derived backend metadata as `backendFamily`, reject raw descriptors that try
  to supply forged `backendFamily` values, and reject otherwise valid rows
  whose ids lack backend-family registration before they can enter the catalog.
  The JS/Python parity guard now compares backend family as part of the public
  descriptor shape, not only the parsed Rust native capability rows, and the
  package declaration guard requires `PrivacyAlgorithmDescriptor.backendFamily`
  to remain readonly in `index.d.ts`. The same parity test now parses the
  private JavaScript source/dist backend-family registration maps and compares
  them, plus Python's `BACKEND_FAMILY_BY_ALGORITHM_ID`, against exact catalog
  row order so stale extra keys, missing keys, reordered rows, and value drift
  are caught.
- The guard now also parses the Rust native privacy production-gate contract in
  those three hosts. It locks the gate version, gate-key/reason tuples,
  supplemental native fail-closed reasons, empty audit references, and the
  `ready: false` / `production_ready: false` payload shape so native
  capabilities cannot drift into a production-looking state independently of
  the SDK catalogs.
- Tightened JavaScript and Python privacy-native availability checks so a
  binding is reported available only after the complete ABI surface returns
  non-empty binary Norito-like archives for capabilities and malformed
  build/verify probes. Text, empty, missing, non-byte, throwing, or coerced ABI
  outputs now fail closed while direct build/verify calls still avoid an extra
  availability probe and continue to clear temporary request copies.
- Added a separate source-level JavaScript privacy FFI contract parity test
  that enforces the stable ABI version, FFI version, status code, null-pointer
  code, malformed-Norito code, unsupported-algorithm code,
  production-disabled code, and invalid-request code across the C bridge,
  JavaScript host, Python PyO3 host, JavaScript source/dist, Python wrapper,
  Swift, Java Android, Kotlin/JVM, and C# bridge declarations. The guard now
  also locks the Norito `PrivacyCapabilitiesV1`, production-gate,
  `PrivacyProofRequestV1`, `PrivacyProofResultV1`, and build/verify operation
  schemas across the C bridge, JavaScript host, and Python PyO3 host. It also
  locks the public C FFI symbol names, Swift `dlsym` lookups, C# `DllImport`
  entry points, and Java/Kotlin JNI privacy bridge method names so binding
  layers cannot drift from the stable production FFI surface. The same guard
  now requires JS, Python, Swift, Java Android, Kotlin/JVM, and C# privacy FFI
  wrappers to expose byte-oriented archive boundaries without JSON request or
  result payloads, and it requires the C bridge, Java JNI adapter, JavaScript
  NAPI host, and Python PyO3 host privacy paths to remain Norito-only and
  JSON-free.
- Hardened Swift, Java Android, Kotlin/JVM, and C# privacy-native availability
  checks to match the JavaScript/Python policy: every SDK now requires the
  capabilities call plus malformed non-empty build/verify proof probes to
  return non-empty native archives before reporting the privacy FFI available.
  The probe archive is the shared
  `iroha-privacy-native-availability-probe-v1` value, copied defensively before
  native dispatch; C# no longer treats the old empty-request `-311` rejection
  as evidence that privacy proving/verifying is available.
- Added Python and JavaScript adversarial catalog guards proving planned
  production privacy SDK entrypoints remain unexported from package roots,
  Python crypto, JavaScript source/dist Node/browser crypto modules, and
  JavaScript source/dist instruction-builder deep modules, and disjoint from
  executable SDK entrypoints until the corresponding production gates pass.
  Rows with planned entrypoints must still report
  `production_ready = false`, `production_gate.ready = false`, and the
  fail-closed reason `planned SDK entrypoints remain`.
- The JavaScript parity guard now also reads the published
  `index.d.ts` declarations plus the Python package export file and the Swift,
  Java Android, Kotlin/JVM, and C# privacy bridge public API sources. It
  rejects exact, PascalCase, and snake_case forms of every planned production
  privacy SDK entrypoint until that row passes the production gate. This keeps
  SDK consumers from seeing a production-looking API before the runtime,
  catalog, native bridge, and audit gates are actually satisfied.
- Extended the JavaScript parity guard so every cataloged executable privacy
  SDK entrypoint must be exported from both source and checked-in dist package
  roots and declared as an exported TypeScript function in `index.d.ts`. This
  closes the inverse SDK drift case where a row advertises an available builder
  but dist or the published type surface silently drops the function.
- Extended the Python native registry guard to bind every SDK-builder/component
  privacy row to its concrete Python module. The guard requires cataloged dev
  SDK entrypoints to remain exported and callable while exact and snake_case
  planned production entrypoints stay absent from module attributes and
  `__all__` until the corresponding production gates pass.
- The same Python guard now checks the `iroha_python` package root: every
  cataloged component dev entrypoint and its module-defined Python alias must
  remain exported and callable from the top-level package, while exact,
  snake_case, and Pythonic planned-production aliases such as `zkat` and
  `verange` stay absent. The JavaScript cross-SDK declaration scanner now uses
  those Pythonic alias forms as well when it checks public API files.
- The Python privacy catalog tests now use the same alias-aware planned-name
  set for package exports, crypto exports, and capability keys, so a
  production-looking `build_zkat_*`, `build_verange_*`, or equivalent planned
  alias cannot appear without failing the production-gate tests.
- Tightened JavaScript source/dist and Python privacy catalog descriptor
  validation so `plannedSdkEntrypoints` / `planned_sdk_entrypoints` cannot
  contain dev-fixture names. Planned entrypoints represent future production
  APIs only; descriptors that try to park `DevFixture` or `DevProofFixture`
  builders in the planned production surface now fail catalog loading, and the
  JS/Python parity guard checks the committed catalogs contain no planned
  dev-fixture entrypoints.
- JavaScript source and checked-in dist tests now lock the direct
  `getPrivacyCapabilities()` runtime object to the four catalog-only keys:
  `javascriptSdkAvailable`, `bridgeAvailable`, `privacyAlgorithms`, and
  `privacyCriteria`. Production-looking status booleans or builder flags must
  stay inside the fail-closed catalog descriptors until the production gates
  pass.
- Browser crypto tests now cover all raw privacy FFI stubs:
  `privacyCapabilitiesV1`, `privacyBuildProofV1`, and `privacyVerifyProofV1`
  must remain unavailable in browser-only bundles, with
  `isPrivacyNativeAvailable()` reporting `false`.
- Added an explicit 64 MiB `PRIVACY_NATIVE_ARCHIVE_MAX_BYTES` /
  `PrivacyNativeArchiveMaxBytes` cap across JavaScript source/dist/browser,
  Python, Swift, Java Android, Kotlin/JVM, and C# privacy native wrappers.
  Direct native calls and availability probes now reject oversized Norito
  archives before reporting the privacy bridge available or returning bytes to
  SDK callers.
- Extended the source-level FFI parity guard so the archive cap must be wired
  into the native-output decoder and availability-probe predicates, not merely
  declared as a public constant. JavaScript source/dist and Python probes must
  route through the capped decoder, while Swift, Java Android, Kotlin/JVM, and
  C# probes must explicitly reject outputs above the shared cap.
- The same guard now locks the browser source/dist JavaScript cap and Swift's
  internal `NativeBridge.privacyNativeArchiveMaxBytes` value, so browser bundles
  and the dynamic library read path cannot drift from the public SDK constant.
- The JavaScript package declaration guard now also requires
  `PRIVACY_NATIVE_ARCHIVE_MAX_BYTES` to remain part of the published
  TypeScript surface, so SDK consumers can rely on the same native archive
  boundary that the runtime wrappers enforce.
- Python privacy-native tests now also require
  `PRIVACY_NATIVE_ARCHIVE_MAX_BYTES` to stay re-exported from the
  `iroha_python` package root and listed in `iroha_python.__all__`, matching
  the public `iroha_python.crypto` constant.
- Expanded JavaScript source/dist and Python availability-probe tests so
  oversized native outputs are rejected independently for capabilities,
  build-proof, and verify-proof probe calls. Python lowers the cap inside the
  test to avoid allocating large archives while still exercising the same
  fail-closed path.
- Added the same 64 MiB encoded-output cap inside the Rust-native privacy FFI
  hosts: the C bridge `write_privacy_payload` path, JavaScript NAPI
  `encode_privacy_archive`, and Python PyO3 `encode_privacy_archive_py` now
  reject oversized Norito result archives before handing bytes to SDK callers.
  The JavaScript FFI parity guard locks the Rust host constants and the
  `bytes.len() > PRIVACY_NATIVE_ARCHIVE_MAX_BYTES` fail-closed branches.
- Extended the same 64 MiB boundary to inbound privacy proof request archives.
  JavaScript and Python reject oversized requests before making temporary
  witness-bearing copies; Swift, Java Android, Kotlin/JVM, and C# reject before
  native dispatch; the C bridge raw pointer reader, C bridge shared JNI
  decoder, JavaScript NAPI host, and Python PyO3 host reject oversized archives
  before Norito decode.
- Added negative request-cap tests across JavaScript source/dist, Python,
  Swift, Java Android, Kotlin/JVM, and C# so oversized proof build/verify
  archives fail before native calls. The source-level FFI parity guard now also
  locks those request-cap branches, not only the output/probe caps.
- Extended SDK privacy native tests so witness-bearing proof request copies are
  also zeroed when native build/verify calls throw. JavaScript source/dist,
  Python, Java Android, Kotlin/JVM, and C# tests now capture temporary request
  buffers on the leaking native-error path, prove they are not aliases of the
  caller's archive, verify native error text still redacts witness material,
  and assert the captured copies are all-zero after the exception path unwinds.
  The source-level FFI parity guard locks that failure-path zeroization
  coverage across those SDK test files.
- Normalized the Rust-native inbound privacy request archive cap into a
  testable `privacy_request_archive_out_of_bounds` predicate in the C bridge,
  JavaScript NAPI host, and Python PyO3 host. Each host now has unit coverage
  for zero-length rejection, one-byte acceptance, exact-cap acceptance, and
  cap-plus-one rejection without allocating an oversized archive, and the
  JavaScript FFI parity guard locks the helper and decoder call sites.
- Added a shared native-side
  `PRIVACY_NATIVE_AVAILABILITY_PROBE_ARCHIVE` constant in the C bridge,
  JavaScript NAPI host, and Python PyO3 host, matching the SDK probe bytes.
  Each host now tests that the exact availability probe decodes to the
  deterministic fail-closed `PRIVACY_FFI_ERROR_MALFORMED_NORITO` result with no
  algorithm, entrypoint, verifier-key, public-input, proof, or verification
  leakage; the JavaScript FFI parity guard locks the native constant and
  malformed-error test policy.
- Tightened JavaScript source/dist and Python privacy FFI wrappers so native
  output archives must be valid Norito V1 frames, not merely non-empty bytes.
  The wrappers now check `NRT0` magic, version `0.0`, supported layout flags,
  declared payload length, bounded zero alignment padding, and CRC64-XZ before
  reporting native privacy availability or returning capability/build/verify
  archives. Source/dist/Python tests now use framed fake native outputs and add
  adversarial rejection coverage for one-byte output, bad magic, bad version,
  unsupported flags, non-zero padding, and bad CRC.
- Extended the same Norito V1 output-frame validation to Swift, Java Android,
  Kotlin/JVM, and C# native privacy bridges. Availability probes and normal
  native output readers now reject arbitrary non-empty bytes unless they have
  `NRT0` magic, version `0.0`, supported layout flags, bounded zero padding,
  declared payload length, and a matching CRC64-XZ checksum. Mobile/JVM/.NET
  tests now use framed archives for positive probes and add adversarial
  rejection coverage for one-byte output, bad magic, bad version, unsupported
  flags, non-zero padding, and bad CRC.
- Closed the Java Android production-gate DTO parity gap by adding an explicit
  empty `auditReferences()` surface to `PrivacyCapabilities`. The field is
  backed by an immutable empty list, the Java harness now rejects forged audit
  signoff insertion through the returned list, and the JavaScript FFI contract
  parity guard requires Java Android to keep the same fail-closed audit
  reference shape as Swift, Kotlin/JVM, and C#.
- Extended the forged-audit-signoff regression across Swift, Kotlin/JVM, and
  C# privacy native tests. Kotlin now uses a named immutable empty
  audit-reference list, Kotlin/C# reject mutation attempts against the returned
  list, Swift proves the value-copy surface cannot retain forged audit
  references, and the source-level parity guard requires every mobile/.NET
  privacy test source to carry the forged audit-reference adversarial marker.
- Hardened the public C# `PrivacyCapabilitiesArchive` and
  `PrivacyProofResultArchive` constructors so callers cannot wrap arbitrary
  non-empty bytes as privacy FFI results. The shared copy path now rejects
  oversized archives and validates the same Norito V1 frame shape used for
  native output decoding before storing a defensive copy. C# tests now use
  valid framed archives for positive wrapper-copy coverage and reject empty,
  malformed, tampered, and oversized public wrapper inputs; the JavaScript FFI
  parity guard locks those source and test expectations because `dotnet` is
  unavailable in this environment.
- Strengthened the cross-SDK frame fixtures so JavaScript source/dist, Python,
  Swift, Java Android, Kotlin/JVM, and C# positive native-output paths now use
  valid Norito frames with a non-empty payload, zero alignment padding, declared
  payload length, and a known CRC64-XZ checksum. The adversarial frame tests now
  also tamper the payload while leaving the checksum unchanged, proving the
  validators are checking payload bytes rather than only header shape.
- Tightened public proof build/verify request handling so JavaScript
  source/dist, Python, Swift, Java Android, Kotlin/JVM, and C# reject invalid
  Norito V1 request archives before native dispatch. Python validates the
  caller-provided memoryview before creating the clearable witness-bearing
  request copy, while C# validates the same clearable request buffer that is
  passed to P/Invoke and wiped in `finally`. Internal availability probes still
  call the native bridge with the shared malformed probe archive to exercise the
  deterministic fail-closed ABI path.
- Added native-host adversarial Norito request-frame fixtures across the C
  bridge, JavaScript NAPI host, and Python PyO3 host. The tests mutate magic,
  version, compression, declared payload length, CRC, flags, payload bytes, and
  truncation cases, and require both build and verify request decoders to
  return the deterministic malformed-Norito result without algorithm,
  verifier-key, public-input, proof, or verification leakage.
- Extended the OpenVerify verifier-backend taxonomy with append-only
  fail-closed tags for the SDK-builder/component privacy families that were
  previously easy to collapse into generic `Stark` or `Unsupported`: Anonymous
  PGC, VeRange, zkAt, recursive anonymous admission/ZK-AMS, Vega existing
  credentials, Silent Threshold anoncreds, ZK-X.509, and SIS-with-hints. Rust
  chain admission now treats those tags as pending production backends, while
  Swift, Java Android, Kotlin/JVM, C#, JavaScript source/dist, TypeScript
  declarations, and the Python OpenVerify codec mirror the labels and parser
  aliases. Jindo remains on the existing `lattice-pcs-sis` family with explicit
  Jindo aliases.
- Closed the remaining Java Android and Kotlin/JVM backend-tag classifier gap.
  Both SDKs now retain exact Norito `parse(...)` behavior for canonical enum
  labels and add catalog-label classifiers plus pending-production predicates,
  matching the Rust/Swift/C# behavior for aliases such as `halo2/ipa/orchard`,
  `groth16/bls12-377`, `penumbra-masp`, `monero-fcmp++`, `stark/fri/miden`,
  `aztec/private-kernel`, `stark/fri/pq-masp-stark-fri`, and component-row
  names. Supported legacy aliases such as `halo2/ipa`, `halo2/bn254`,
  `groth16`, and `stark/fri/sha256-goldilocks` remain non-pending. Their
  focused tests now also mirror the Swift/C# adversarial alias set, including
  bare `orchard`, `anonymous-pgc-k-out-of-n`, `verange-transparent-range`,
  `zkAt policy-private authenticator`, `threshold-anonymous-credentials`,
  `post-quantum-masp`, `halo2/pasta/ipa/vote-bool`, `groth16/bn254`, plain
  `stark`, and unknown slash-shaped backend labels.
- Added cross-SDK adversarial backend-label coverage for punctuation-spliced
  pending privacy labels. Java Android and Kotlin/JVM now prove that labels
  such as `halo2/ipa/orchard/dev-fixture`,
  `stark/fri/miden/claimed-production`,
  `anonymous-pgc-k-out-of-n-v1-production`,
  `sis-hints-anoncred-pq-v0-devfixture`,
  `groth16/bls12-377/../../prod`, and
  `post-quantum-masp/audit-claimed` classify as exact pending families for
  fail-closed guards but cannot parse as canonical Norito backend tags. Swift
  and C# carry the same fail-closed catalog-classifier regression coverage.
  The JavaScript FFI parity guard now locks this adversarial label set across
  JS, Python, Java Android, Kotlin/JVM, Swift, and C# test sources so the
  near-miss pending-backend coverage cannot drift per SDK.
- Closed the JavaScript/Python OpenVerify runtime alias gap for pending
  privacy backend labels. The JS source/dist envelope builders and Norito
  encoder plus the Python OpenVerify codec now compact labels with the same
  ASCII-alphanumeric rule and preserve catalog-shaped aliases such as
  `zcash-orchard`, `bls12-377`, `decaf377`, `monero-fcmp++`,
  `jindo-lattice-pcs-zk-v0`, `stark/fri/miden`,
  `stark/fri/pq-masp-stark-fri`, `anonymous-pgc-k-out-of-n-v1`,
  `verange-transparent-range-v1`, `zkat-policy-private-auth-v1`,
  `recursive-anonymous-admission-v0`, `vega-existing-credential-zk-v0`,
  `silent-threshold-anoncred-v0`, `zk-x509-onchain-identity-v0`, and
  `sis-hints-anoncred-pq-v0` as their exact pending enum families instead of
  rejecting or collapsing them into generic backends. The same JS/Python tests
  now reject punctuation-spliced suffix labels such as Orchard dev fixtures,
  claimed-production Miden labels, production-suffixed Anonymous PGC ids,
  dev-fixture SIS hints, and path-spliced BLS12-377 labels after compacting, so
  broader normalization cannot silently admit near-miss aliases.
- Hardened the BOI Privacy Lab catalog regression coverage for SDK-only rows
  that claim production status. A cataloged SDK research target that supplies
  every production-gate flag, a valid audit reference, and a dev-fixture
  entrypoint now has explicit tests proving the BOI runner still surfaces it as
  unavailable and production-blocked because there is no BOI execution adapter,
  planned SDK entrypoints remain, dev fixtures are not production entrypoints,
  and the BOI production allowlist is not enabled.
- Closed verifier-key registry admission for those pending protocol families.
  `RegisterVerifyingKey` and `UpdateVerifyingKey` now reject direct pending
  `BackendTag`s and raw verifier-key id backend labels that parse to pending
  families before WSV writes or circuit-index updates, so labels such as
  `halo2/ipa/orchard`, `stark/fri/miden`, and component rows cannot be admitted
  as generic Halo2/STARK verifier keys. OpenVerify backend matching now uses
  the same pending-production parser instead of a hand-maintained label list.
- Closed the matching proof-use boundary for legacy/imported state. Generic
  `VerifyProof` now rejects pending-production proof backend labels before
  registry lookup, and rejects active verifier records whose stored backend tag
  is a pending family before preverified-cache lookup or native verification.
  Adversarial tests seed those records directly into WSV to prove a stale
  registry entry cannot bypass admission by relying on a cached preverify hit.
- Closed the block-level transaction attachment preverify boundary as well.
  Attachment preverify now rejects pending-production proof backend labels
  before WSV lookup, and rejects stale WSV verifier records carrying pending
  backend tags before computing preverified results. Focused attachment tests
  cover raw pending labels plus direct legacy-state verifier records.
- Closed the IVM contract-host verifier snapshot boundary. `CoreHost`
  hydration now rejects pending-production verifier record tags and pending raw
  backend labels before exposing WSV verifier keys to contract syscalls. Host
  tests cover pending labels such as Orchard/Miden/PQ-MASP and direct pending
  `BackendTag` records.
- Closed the offline transparent verifier-resolution boundary. Offline note
  recursive proofs and Kagemusha transfer/redeem resolver paths now reject
  pending-production proof labels before registry/state lookup, and reject
  stale verifier records carrying pending backend tags before proof decode or
  native verification. Adversarial tests cover every pending backend tag plus
  catalog labels such as Orchard, Penumbra MASP, FCMP++, Jindo/lattice,
  Miden, Aztec, PQ MASP, Anonymous PGC, VeRange, zkAt, ZK-AMS, Vega, Silent
  Threshold, ZK-X.509, and SIS-with-hints.
- Closed the low-level verifier-dispatch boundary. `zk.rs` now exposes a
  shared pending-production backend-label classifier and rejects those labels
  before STARK/FRI family classification, preverify dedup, plain native
  verifier dispatch, and guardrailed verifier dispatch. Direct negative tests
  cover prefix-shaped labels such as `halo2/ipa/orchard`, `stark/fri/miden`,
  and `stark/fri/pq-masp-stark-fri` so cataloged-but-unaudited engines cannot
  be normalized into broad Halo2/STARK verifier families by lower-level callers.
- Closed the native privacy FFI planned-entrypoint boundary. The C bridge,
  JavaScript NAPI host, and Python PyO3 host now keep `planned_entrypoints` as
  capability metadata only; request dispatch accepts only concrete
  `sdk_entrypoints`, while planned production builders/verifiers return a
  deterministic invalid-request result before vk_ref, witness, proof, or
  production-gate validation. The parity test now checks all three native
  hosts keep planned entrypoints out of the executable allowlist.
- The JavaScript FFI parity guard now locks Swift, Kotlin/JVM, C#, and Java
  Android privacy capability DTOs to coarse fail-closed model shapes. Swift,
  Kotlin, and C# may expose only SDK availability, bridge availability,
  `productionReady`, and the production gate; Java Android may expose only the
  coarse production-gate booleans and missing reasons. Per-algorithm builder or
  production-looking capability fields remain rejected until the audited
  production gates pass.
- The same FFI parity guard now locks Swift, Java Android, Kotlin/JVM, and C#
  native privacy wrapper methods to generic archive operations only:
  capabilities plus build/verify proof archive calls. Per-algorithm planned
  proof builders such as Orchard, Penumbra, FCMP++, Miden, Aztec, PQ MASP, or
  component-row builders cannot appear on those wrapper method surfaces before
  the production gate.
- Extended those guards to the capability surfaces themselves. Python now
  rejects exact planned-entrypoint capability keys and known production-status
  aliases such as `asset_hidden_transfer_proof_v1`,
  `anonymous_pgc_k_out_of_n_proof_v1`, `orchard_action_bundle_proof_v1`,
  `pq_masp_stark_transfer_proof_v0`, and `ml_kem_note_encryption` unless they
  are absent or explicitly `false`; JavaScript source and checked-in dist
  capabilities likewise cannot expose planned entrypoints under canonical,
  PascalCase, snake_case, `ve_range`/`verange`, or `zk_at`/`zkat` alias forms,
  and JavaScript source/dist runtime exports must keep those same variants
  absent from package, crypto, browser-crypto, and instruction-builder module
  surfaces. The Python catalog test now also locks the top-level
  `privacy_capabilities()` key set to the current cataloged SDK/dev-fixture
  surface so any new production-looking capability flag must be reviewed
  through the production gate instead of appearing silently.
- The parity guard keeps all cataloged privacy rows fail-closed until real Rust
  proving/verifying engines, chain admission, wallet/state support,
  deterministic tests, fuzzing, performance gates, and external audit signoff
  are present.

## 2026-06-02 Kagemusha recursive redemption lineage gate

- Added a data-model redeem preflight guard for the current Reserved-lineage
  circuit boundary: witnessless Reserved-lineage redeem requests now fail before
  heavy proof work with `lineage_witness`. Record-backed lineage witnesses
  remain the required online redemption path for every hop.
- Exposed
  `KAGEMUSHA_RECURSIVE_SPEND_LINEAGE_WITNESSLESS_MAX_HOPS_V1 = 0` in the Rust
  data model and Swift, Kotlin/JVM, Java Android, JavaScript/Node, Python, and
  C# SDK surfaces. Wallets can use this stable bound to keep the record-backed
  lineage witness for every online recursive redemption.
- Added SDK-facing circuit-id/hop-count helpers for the same decision:
  witnessless redeem is currently rejected for semantic v1, unknown circuits,
  zero-hop, and Reserved-lineage hop counts; online redemption requires the
  record-backed lineage witness path until the production lineage circuit is
  wired.
- Extended `KagemushaRecursiveSpendVerifyResultV1` with defaulted
  `witnessless_redeem_supported` and
  `lineage_witness_required_for_redeem` booleans. Native verify archives now
  tell wallets whether redeem can be witnessless without requiring SDKs to
  decode the recursive bundle circuit id themselves.
- Added data-model coverage for the Reserved-lineage redeem boundary:
  witnessless Reserved-lineage redeem rejects with `lineage_witness`.
- Tightened core Halo2 IPA backend dispatch for the Reserved-lineage key path:
  the one-hop verifier-slice branch now rejects forged multi-hop metadata,
  witness-count splices, zero scalar-projection columns, and non-zero public
  padding before selecting a lineage verifier key.
- Hardened recursive spend accumulator coverage for Reserved-lineage previous
  proof artifacts: scalar-projection substitutions now have explicit regression
  coverage showing they are bound into the next proof-chain digest, while a
  zero scalar projection is rejected before append.
- Added a dedicated Kagemusha payload benchmark CI workflow and helper script.
  The workflow runs the existing reduced-sample
  `kagemusha_recursive_spend_payload` Criterion bench on relevant accumulator,
  payload, and proof-surface changes and uploads the summary artifact.
- Updated JavaScript and Python SDK wrapper tests so native witnessless
  Reserved-lineage rejection is propagated as a no-output/native rejection
  instead of fallback bytes. This keeps SDK error propagation aligned with the
  data-model and ledger preflight boundary.
- Changed ABI-6 native append for the C bridge, JavaScript/Node host, and Python
  PyO3 host so appending from a Reserved-lineage previous proof verifies that
  previous proof with `previous_lineage_verifier_record`, then emits the
  semantic `kagemusha-recursive-aggregation-v1` spend bundle for the appended
  state. That avoids asking the Reserved-lineage verifier-slice circuit to prove
  hop 2+ and keeps SDK D2D payloads hop-count-independent across offline
  re-spends.
- Kept the Reserved-lineage redemption profile fail-closed for chain admission:
  bundles with strict verifier-slice columns are still D2D/profile-verifiable,
  but witnessless redemption rejects after profile validation until the
  production recursive lineage circuit proves private hop lineage and
  accumulator transitions in-circuit. Semantic v1 recursive spend proofs can
  still be used for receiver-side offline verification, but ledger redemption
  requires a record-backed lineage witness.
- The redeem execution path now verifies supplied lineage witnesses against
  active verifier records and replays the accumulator before final unshield
  admission. Native bridge, JavaScript host, Python PyO3, Swift, Kotlin/JVM,
  Java Android, and C# surfaces propagate native no-output failures for
  malformed, backend-invalid, or witnessless lineage payloads instead
  of synthesizing fallback instruction bytes.
- Filled compile and portability gaps discovered during focused validation:
  base `World::bind_contract_alias` keeps contract alias indexes consistent for
  existing sponsored-contract tests, Apple/backend mapping only accepts
  supported Kagemusha record curves, and the Norito XCFramework builder passes
  `--lib` so Swift bridge builds do not compile unrelated binaries.
- Tightened SDK output handling beyond empty/null archives: JavaScript and
  Python now reject native text returns instead of coercing or indirectly
  failing them as byte archives, JavaScript treats a throwing bridge ABI probe
  as unavailable recursive-spend support, and C# now rejects zero-length success
  buffers before trying to marshal or free native output pointers.

## 2026-06-02 Python SIS-with-hints SDK parity

- Added Python SDK SIS-with-hints anonymous credential helpers matching the
  already-cataloged JavaScript surface:
  `buildSisHintsCredentialCommitments`, `buildSisHintsCredentialEnvelope`,
  `buildSisHintsCredentialDevProofFixture`, and
  `verifySisHintsCredentialProofLocally`, plus snake-case Python aliases.
- The helpers derive deterministic dev issuer, credential, showing-policy, and
  parameter public inputs from canonical structured material; accept externally
  generated public inputs and prepared proof bytes; emit shared
  `OpenVerifyEnvelope` Norito frames; and intentionally require the
  `Unsupported` backend until a production SIS-with-hints verifier backend is
  registered. No production lattice anonymous-credential prover or verifier was
  added.
- Added Python adversarial coverage for mismatched or zero public-input
  commitments, missing issuer/credential/policy/parameter material, blank
  domains, unsupported versions, ambiguous aliases, oversized source material,
  unknown fields, wrong backend/circuit id, zero verifier hash, empty or
  oversized proof bytes, arbitrary/tampered dev proof bytes, issuer/credential/
  policy/parameter/domain substitution, verifier-key substitution,
  noncanonical public-input JSON, zero public-input issuer commitments, and
  public-input alias collisions.

## 2026-06-02 Kagemusha recursive lineage prover SDK defaults

- Promoted the reserved `kagemusha-recursive-spend-lineage-v1` path from a
  metadata-only profile to the ABI-6 init default for the native C bridge,
  JavaScript/Node NAPI host, and Python PyO3 host. The hosts derive the Pallas
  open-envelope width from the raw Norito archive, select the matching
  no-trusted-setup one-hop lineage verifier key, and emit a first-hop
  Reserved-lineage bundle. ABI-6 append now verifies that Reserved-lineage
  previous proof with the supplied active lineage verifier record, then emits
  the semantic recursive aggregation spend proof for the appended state so the
  D2D bundle remains multi-hop spendable while witnessless multi-hop lineage
  output remains fail-closed.
- Added a core helper that validates the Pallas open-envelope archive before
  selecting the lineage verifier-key specialization, so SDKs continue to pass
  raw Norito archives and do not reimplement proof internals.
- Added Rust-facing lineage-default init wrappers and routed native init through
  them. Native append now calls the generic recursive append helper with the
  canonical semantic verifier key after validating Reserved-lineage previous
  record selection, keeping semantic v1 proving as the multi-hop compatibility
  path until the production witnessless lineage verifier is wired.
- Moved the large-stack protection for one-hop lineage verifier-key generation
  into the production key builder after the ignored valid-key test showed the
  default caller stack can overflow before keygen starts. First-use verifier-key
  materialization now runs on the same large-stack path as the heavy verifier
  tests.
- Hardened record-backed lineage preverification so reserved-lineage proof
  envelopes must include the appended one-hop verifier-slice public instance
  columns, while semantic-only public-instance envelopes remain compatibility
  material for semantic v1 preverification only.
- Added helper-level adversarial coverage for empty, malformed, and
  opening-length-spliced Pallas archives, plus an ignored large-stack valid-path
  test that generates the production one-hop lineage verifier key from a real
  Pallas archive.

## 2026-06-02 Kagemusha lineage-witness append boundary hardening

- Hardened the recursive spend lineage-witness helper tests so append assembly
  rejects a request whose `previous_bundle` no longer matches the carried
  witness, rejects chain/asset-spliced one-hop append fragments, and rejects a
  stale appended bundle before returning redeem witness material. The helper
  also now rejects reserved-lineage bundles at init, previous-bundle append,
  and appended-bundle append boundaries so witnessless lineage proofs stay on
  the verifier-record-backed path.
- This pins the accumulator handoff between D2D append proving and separate
  redeem-side lineage witness storage: helper callers cannot splice a valid
  one-hop record fragment into a witness bound to a different chain, asset,
  previous recursive spend bundle, or final recursive spend bundle.
- Direct redeem-request validation now rejects reserved-lineage bundles that
  carry record-backed witness material, keeping the witnessless lineage profile
  on its verifier-record-backed admission path.
- Added explicit data-model preflight for recursive spend init, append, and
  verify request archives. Init preflight rejects malformed one-hop fragments,
  bad Pallas archive counts, verifier-record set issues, and spendable note
  output/nullifier splices. Append preflight additionally rejects previous proof
  attachment drift, missing/forbidden previous lineage verifier records,
  malformed previous lineage record metadata, chain/asset/root discontinuity,
  amount drift, missing previous-note nullifier consumption, and top-up-anchor
  output reuse before recursive proving starts.
- Routed the native bridge and SDK init/append entry points through the new
  request preflight so malformed Norito archives fail consistently before
  Halo2 proving-key construction or native output bytes are returned.
- Routed record-backed lineage-witness assembly through the same init/append
  request preflight before merging hop envelopes or carrying previous recursive
  proofs, so redeem-side witness material cannot be built from an append request
  that the recursive prover would reject.
- Added reserved-previous-with-active-lineage-record coverage for witness
  assembly: append preflight accepts the reserved previous proof only with a
  matching active lineage verifier record, and malformed or forged records still
  reject before redeem instruction construction.
- Reordered recursive redeem execution so final unshield/redeem proof public
  binding is checked before reserved-lineage chain-admission and backend proof
  verification. This preserves the final spendable-note mismatch diagnostic for
  tampered final proofs and keeps malformed lineage-key metadata from masking
  that gate.
- The native bridge adversarial redeem-witness test now covers the same
  reserved-lineage-with-record-witness splice at the raw Norito archive
  boundary. JavaScript/Node and Python PyO3 native host tests mirror that case
  so SDK host helpers reject the same invalid combination before returning
  instruction bytes.

## 2026-06-02 Kagemusha reserved-lineage redeem fail-closed restoration

  in-circuit.

  fail-closed chain redeem candidate after strict metadata/profile validation.
  Semantic v1 remains admission-neutral without a record-backed lineage witness,
  while witnessless reserved-lineage requests now reject even when they carry

  proof verification now returns success again instead of falling through to the
  reserved-lineage sentinel.

  reserved-lineage redeem requests rejected with the then-current
  lineage-circuit-not-wired diagnostic, while missing verifier-slice columns,
  zero scalar projections, and malformed lineage envelopes still rejected

  backend, and canonical curve label before proof decoding. Record-backed
  lineage witnesses now reject inactive, namespace-spliced, backend-spliced,
  wrong-curve, empty-circuit, zero-schema, zero-commitment, proof-cap, key-length,
  and inline-key mismatches at the data-model boundary; chain-side
  `KagemushaTransfer`, compact-token record verification, recursive aggregation
  record preverification, and final recursive redeem/unshield admission now
  reject Halo2 IPA records that claim a non-`pallas` curve. Final recursive
  redeem/unshield admission also requires the verifier record to live in the
  `offline_kagemusha` namespace and be the active circuit/version binding before

  key substitutions that do not match the canonical confidential unshield
  circuit key.

  previous bundle and to keep witnessless reserved-lineage redeem serialization
  fail-closed until the production lineage circuit is wired.

## 2026-06-03 Swift Ethereum SCCP outbound prover preflight

- Tightened the Swift `EthereumMainnetSccp.proveOutboundToEthereum` facade so
  it now builds and validates the Ethereum-mainnet-only outbound proof request
  before invoking the app-owned Groth16 prover callback. BSC-targeted or
  non-SORA-source requests therefore fail at the facade boundary instead of
  reaching local prover code and being rejected only after proof wrapping.

  facade does not call the configured prover closure, and added release
  verifier/readiness inventory guards so that pre-callback regression remains
  part of the published SDK evidence set.

## 2026-06-03 Ethereum SCCP source-adapter shape hardening

- Tightened the Ethereum beacon receipt source-adapter preflight so malformed
  proofs with empty execution headers, empty sync committee rosters, or
  mismatched sync committee roster/weight/PoP vectors are rejected by the shape
  gate before admission or cryptographic verification. The same gate now also
  rejects zero total/signed committee weights, zero per-validator weights, and
  all-zero signer bitmaps; it also rejects impossible `signed_weight >
  total_weight` claims and signer bitmaps with bits outside the advertised
  roster. Zero sync-committee message hashes are rejected at the same preflight
  boundary.
- Extended the EVM source-adapter preflight regression to cover those malformed
  Ethereum shapes alongside the existing oversized receipt proof, committee,
  and transition cases.
- Tightened Ethereum sync-committee transition preflight as well: transition
  records now need version/domain consistency, adjacent sync periods, a
  period-matching nonzero transition slot, nonzero roots/hashes, bounded next
  committee payloads, and a well-formed signing committee before the transition
  chain reaches cryptographic verification.
- Added top-level Ethereum beacon-receipt adapter preflight checks for
  version/domain consistency and nonzero finality, execution, sync-committee,
  and receipt-proof hashes so incomplete source-proof envelopes fail before
  admission binding.
- Validation:
  - `cargo fmt --all` (passed)
  - `cargo test -p iroha_sccp evm_family_source_adapter_preflight_rejects_oversized_shapes -- --nocapture`
    (`1` passed)

    (`1` passed)

    (`1` passed)

## 2026-06-03 SoraNet PQ ML-KEM canonical key admission

- Hardened `soranet_pq` ML-KEM key validation so exact-length public keys and
  secret-key private components are decoded as 12-bit polynomial coefficients
  and rejected when any coefficient is outside the FIPS 203 field range
  `q = 3329`.
- `validate_secret_key`, `public_key_from_secret_key`, and `decapsulate_mlkem`
  now apply canonical checks to both the private decapsulation-key component and
  the embedded public key before verifying the embedded `H(ek)` hash or invoking
  backend decapsulation.

  `ERR_ENCODING`, and streaming Kyber key admission treats the new ML-KEM error
  shape as invalid key material before snapshot or HPKE state can be installed.
  Streaming regressions now cover noncanonical Kyber public keys and local
  secrets at both key-material and session admission boundaries.
- Hybrid KEM decode regressions now cover the same noncanonical Kyber public and
  secret-key component failures before SoraFS envelope material can be accepted.

## 2026-06-03 SoraNet PQ ML-DSA secret-key consistency

- Hardened `soranet_pq` ML-DSA secret-key validation so length-valid secrets
  are unpacked, re-derived as `t = A*s1 + s2`, checked against the embedded
  `t0`, reconstructed into a public key, checked against embedded
  `tr = H(pk)`, and re-packed to reject noncanonical encodings.
- `sign_mldsa` and `sign_mldsa_from_os` now run the same consistency check
  before signing randomness is consumed or backend signing starts, and
  `mldsa_public_key_from_secret_key` exposes fallible public-key reconstruction
  for callers that need the committed verifier material.
- The C FFI maps the new ML-DSA secret-key consistency failure to
  `ERR_ENCODING`, preserving the existing malformed-input boundary contract.

## 2026-06-03 Ethereum SCCP receipt-trie SDK adversarial hardening

  builders rejecting noncanonical receipt keys and malformed block-receipt
  material: noncanonical JSON-RPC quantities, wrong receipt order,

## 2026-06-03 Streaming ML-KEM local key-pair binding

  public key and `H(ek)` hash embedded in the FIPS 203 decapsulation key and
  rejects length-valid public/secret material that is not one internally
  consistent key pair.

  `StreamingSession::set_kyber_local_key_pair` now reject mismatched local Kyber
  key pairs or `H(ek)`-corrupted secret keys at admission instead of allowing
  implicit-rejection decapsulation to surface later as a transport-key mismatch.

  `decapsulate_mlkem` now also reject secret keys whose embedded `H(ek)` hash
  does not match the embedded public key.

  metadata to match an already-installed local decapsulation secret before any
